messages:
mike: heads-up — saw a sustained exporter backlog from region-eu yesterday, caused retention delta to spike and a bunch of tenant alerts. wondering if we should add a quota-overlay to the sampling controller so routes can opt into stricter head-sampling during backpressure :thinking:
mina: can you paste the logs/metric? is this exporter backlog causing span drops or just delayed delivery?
eli: looks like queue-depth grew then exporters started 5xxing. retention increased because tail-sampler kept more spans while the head sampler was overwhelmed. gist: exporter backpressure -> we keep more to avoid losing tail signals -> cost spike.
mike: exact. proposal: sampling controller gets a per-route "emergency_quota" override that temporarily tightens head sampling (and reduces prefetch) when exporter queue depth > THRESH. Policy should be annotatable by customer_tier.
tanya: +1 in principle. couple constraints: (1) we shouldn't mutate span payloads arbitrarily (customers care about attributes), (2) console UX needs a reversible override and clear cost impact estimate before toggling.
eli: on point (1) — instead of adding fields to span proto, push sampling hints as exporter-level metadata in our OTLP envelope (collector attribute) so downstream storage doesn't see it as customer data. simple and reversible.
mina: how would algorithms decide head vs tail? if we tighten head sampling we risk losing error signals for low-volume routes. maybe only do it for routes with tier==best_effort or where SLO says latency < X.
ralph: suggestion: maintain 3 signals in controller — route_recent_qps, exporter_queue_depth, route_error_rate. emergency_quota = f(qps, queue_depth, error_rate, customer_tier). default f is conservative.
mike: config sketch:

```
route_overrides:
  - route: "/api/v1/generate"
    tier: standard
    emergency_quota:
      enabled: true
      queue_depth_threshold: 2000
      head_sample_rate: 0.02
      fallback: keep_tail_for_errors: true
```

eli: love the sketch. implementation question: exporter backpressure signal — should collector emit a metric we consume, or should exporters push a 429/503 header we parse?
tanya: we have both but the most reliable is collector-side metric (queue_depth and age). parsing 503s is brittle across exporter implementations.
mina: dashboard ask: Console should show per-route "potential cost savings" and "estimated signal loss" for toggling emergency_quota. not just raw tokens/spans. UX should recommend a canary rollout (10% traffic) before global.
ralph: operationally we need a safe default: emergency_quota off for enterprise, opt-in only via console or api flag for tenant admins. platform can enable for internal system routes.
ingest-bot: notice: created metric alert exporter:queue_depth:region-eu > 1500 (auto) — linked incident INC-3421
mike: good call. next steps I propose: (1) add collector metric export for queue_depth and age if missing, (2) implement controller hook to compute emergency_quota per-route, (3) API + console toggle with canary rollout, (4) RFC + small POC for 2 routes. I'll file issues.
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: canary/telemetry-sampler v0.3 -> infra-staging @ 1748894000 — logs: https://ci.redwood/inv/telemetry-canary\tanya: note for RFC — include decision about not modifying customer spans and instead using envelope metadata, and include retention cost model (tokens -> $).
eli: also add a small eval: compare error-detection recall with tightened head sampling on a synthetic traffic replay (we should be able to simulate).
mike: agreed. I'll open the RFC and assign owners: mina (controller), tanya (console UX), eli (collector/metrics), ralph (ops guardrails).
mike: thanks all — let's sync next Wed after RFC draft. :thumbsup:
